newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai president sees sales recovering.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai president sees sales recovering.

text.p: The president of South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday he was confident of achieving its 1997 sales target of 1.4 million vehicles against 1.31 million a year earlier.
Park Byung-jae also told reporters he believed domestic sales would recover from a slump early this year.

"Our domestic sales are recovering this month and I see no problem in meeting the sales target for this year," Park told a news conference, held on the occasion of the 1997 Seoul Motor Show that opens on Thursday.
The company, flagship unit of the Hyundai Group HYGR.CN, aims to sell 800,000 vehicles at home and 600,000 abroad.
Hyundai Motor said earlier this month its vehicle sales in March fell 7.6 percent to 101,957 units from 110,329 units a year earlier.
The company has attributed the sluggish monthly sales to a slowing economy and introduction of new models by its rival Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of the Daewoo Group.
Park said Hyundai has been seeking to build more assembly facilities abroad, especially in eastern Europe.
Hyundai is producing or plans to assemble vehicles in 12 countries, including Turkey, India and Indonesia.
Its Turkey venture to assemble 50,000 vehicles a year is due to begin operations in July and a 120,000-units-a-year India project in October next year, Park said.
